Because the first settlers were Dutch and did not keep particularly clear records and the English first mention of Rhode Island refers to "Rhodos Island", which looks like the "Isle of Rhodes (Ρόδος)". The names of the Dutch towns are known but "Rhode" has a perfectly clear Dutch origin, even though it never got written down in Dutch.

Did the Dutch named Aquidneck Island the "Red Island" (perhaps because of maple trees) or the did English named some island (perhaps Aquidneck, perhaps Conanicut, perhaps Prudence, but also even Block Island or Martha's Vineyard) after a famous, but far off island from Classical antiquity?
